notes: Dev-split ABox revision on captained_national_team (new relation, staging/people.RELATIONS.md: subproperty of played_for_national_team). After review neither relation is tagged functional: FIFA has let players represent two countries (Di Stéfano for Argentina and Spain; one-time switches since 2020), so both are many-valued in general, and per RELATIONS.md's tag rule the record states the presupposition instead: Messi represented one country at senior level (he did: Argentina), so after the edit he captained and played for France only. The edit carries subproperty (related near: captaining a team implies playing for it, asked as a different relation than the edit) and inheritance (derived application: once Messi is one of France's players, the class rule that every France player holds French nationality gives the nationality that made him eligible). Related far asks, as an open question, which continental championship the team he captained competes in (composition on the new value, derivation none); it was a forced choice between the Copa América and the Euros labelled inheritance, which reviewers rightly called a binary guess and not a class rule. A chain label (played_for ∘ competes_in ⊑ played_in) was considered and not used: a player of a team need not have played in every tournament it enters, so that chain does not hold in general. Its original answer is stored (Messi's Argentina at the Copa América). Derived: a binding through the nickname 'La Pulga', a composition on France's capital, and the nationality application. The anthem question was dropped: both teams' anthems are played before an international match, so it had no single answer. Past tense is used because Messi's Wikipedia lead now speaks of his national-team career in the past. A record holder for the Ballon d'Or was considered for the binding but dropped: the award's French name could hint at France. A shirt-colour question was dropped because 'Messi in sky blue and white' is common text, so its answer is stored rather than worked out. Audit fix 2026-11-12: the continental-championship question was replaced by the team's nickname (original La Albiceleste, after the edit Les Bleus): three models answered CONMEBOL, South America or UEFA, and two missed the France bridge, so the question measured wording more than the edit. Both nicknames are stored (first sentence of the Argentina article; second paragraph of the France lead). One related question (2026-11-14, user decision): kept "For which country's national football team did Lionel Messi play?" (stored: see its evidence); dropped the second reading of the same fact.
